p1_second_job_integration_admission.was: the integration lane held ONE configured worker whose own deployment named the FIRST Job's Work and input manifest, so `_disagreements` found 'the Work' and 'the submitted input' for every other Job and `_job_workers` refused job-b/integration before reserve. The predecessor made that refusal the expected outcome.
p1_second_job_integration_admission.investigated_first: whether one capacity identity and one actor can carry per-Job held operations through existing seams, as the review directed. They can: `single_worker.worker_operations` takes a held deployment per call and `PooledManagerOperations` keys ONE operations object per (generation, worker id), so the per-Job selection fits under the existing pool entry with no scheduler, provider, driver or registry change.
p1_second_job_integration_admission.now: `_served_deployment(given, worker, binding)` answers the held deployment a worker actually serves a Job's stage under. For every role but integration, and for the one-Job `/1` document, it is the configured deployment unchanged. For an integration worker under a bound Job it is that deployment with its `input_manifest` taken from the Job's bound `source_worker_id` producer -- the same producer identity `Integration.required_tests` already derives from and the same manifest `_correspondent` compares the Job's own input digest against. `_job_workers` reads it for compatibility and `_integration_operations` composes the provider from it, so admission and `single_worker._matches` read ONE document.
p1_second_job_integration_admission.capacity_unchanged: the pool still carries exactly one integration worker under one `integrator_participant`; `scheduler.own_pool`'s one-participant rule and `scheduler.reserve`'s one-live-allocation-per-worker rule are untouched, so two Jobs' integration stages serialize over that one capacity and the second is refused for CAPACITY when the first holds it -- proved as its own case.
p1_second_job_integration_admission.not_derived: participant, principal, profile name, profile digest and policy digest stay the one configured deployment fact. Substituting a policy or a profile for a Job would be this assembly quietly choosing a security operand; a Job the configured integrator does not carry those for is still refused before anything is reserved, naming the operand.
p1_second_job_integration_admission.adapter: `_PerJobIntegration` selects the per-Job operations by the stage's own `job_id` for admit/claim/launch/dispatch/conclude/observe/refresh_runtime, and answers the deployment-scoped questions -- canonical operation identity, journal read, restart settlement, offer republication and transport pump -- from ONE entry, because every entry is the same participant and control store and `attach`/`drain` must name the same event queue. One binding composes exactly the single operations object it always did, so no `/1` composition changes.

p2_evidence_corrections.receipts: `admitted()`'s `LIKE '%admit%'` scan of the JOB store's operations table is gone. `receipted()` reads the canonical admit receipt at its own owner through `composed.canonical_operation('admit', offer_id)` and `composed.receipt_of(...)`, and asks EVERY episode of the stage rather than only the live one -- an offer identity is derived from the stage and its episode, so a stage that has moved on carries a live episode nobody admitted. Every absence assertion is paired with a positive control that finds a receipt.
p2_evidence_corrections.allocations: `allocations()`'s `SELECT * FROM stage_allocations` is gone. `allocated()` reads the live episode through `live_of` and asks `scheduler.allocation_of` about the attempt it actually names.
p2_evidence_corrections.integration_positive: the case no longer calls `_job_workers` directly. `standalone()`/`offered()`/`attempted()`/`admitting()` submit a Job and admit its stage through `StageExecution.admit` itself -- the reviewer's own probe shape -- and both Jobs' integration admissions are measured as an allocation plus a canonical receipt.
p2_evidence_corrections.fault_capacity: the control now measures the REVIEW worker the incompatible review stage actually threatened: with job-b's reviewer left on Work A, job-b/review is refused with no allocation and no receipt, and job-a/review still reserves `review-worker` and records its own canonical offer afterwards.
p2_evidence_corrections.reconstruction: no SQL. A first composition admits job-b/review publicly and the scheduler really reserves `review-worker-b`; a second composition over the SAME stores exchanges the two reviewers' bound Jobs -- an ordinary redeployment -- and `StageExecution.admit` refuses against the recorded allocation, adding and removing nothing.
